description:
Location: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:74-78

The ChatBackend::generate_invite_code trait doc currently reads:
  /// Generate a cryptographically random invite code.
  ///
  /// Implementations MUST use a CSPRNG (e.g. `rand::thread_rng`, `getrandom`,
  /// OS entropy). The returned string must be unguessable — do NOT use
  /// timestamps or sequential counters.

CONCERN
`rand::thread_rng` is NOT documented as a CSPRNG. The rand crate
documentation describes ThreadRng as 'an automatically-seeded, cryptographically
secure thread-local random number generator' starting in rand 0.9, but in older
versions (and per the rand book) the explicit, stable, supported CSPRNG
recommendation for security-relevant work is OsRng / getrandom. The trait
docstring leads every implementor to a stdlib RNG that the rand crate's own
docs route around for cryptographic use cases. Worse, the historical
ThreadRng implementation has been changed before (StdRng → ChaCha) and is
explicitly described as implementation-defined; using it for an invite code
inherits future churn risk for free.

Invite codes are unguessable-secret material: an attacker who can predict
the code can hijack a Space invitation. This is exactly the class of use
case where the trait doc should point implementors at OsRng / getrandom,
not at thread_rng.

The default MemoryBackend impl at memory.rs:517 and the test backend at
tests/common/mod.rs:136 BOTH explicitly note 'test-only: not a CSPRNG'
and use nanosecond timestamps — they are correctly labeled as
test-only. The bug is only in the trait doc-comment that guides every
*production* implementor.

PROPOSED FIX
Change the trait docstring to:
  /// Implementations MUST use a CSPRNG. `rand::rngs::OsRng` or the
  /// `getrandom` crate are the recommended choices. Do NOT use
  /// `rand::thread_rng()` for security-relevant output — it is a
  /// fast PRNG whose CSPRNG status is implementation-defined, and
  /// the rand crate docs route security-sensitive callers to OsRng.

RISK CLASSIFICATION
P2 (defense-in-depth). No production code in this workspace actually
generates invite codes — only test stubs. But this is a public trait
doc-comment guiding every downstream backend implementor, and the
guidance is wrong. Better to fix before the first production
implementation lands.

ORACLE
- rand crate documentation for OsRng vs ThreadRng (https://docs.rs/rand)
- CFRG / IRTF guidance: cryptographic invite codes must come from a
  CSPRNG with documented OS-level entropy seeding, not from a
  thread-local PRNG with implementation-defined seeding semantics
title: Security: ChatBackend::generate_invite_code doc-comment falsely claims rand::thread_rng is a CSPRNG
